newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARIA PLANS TO KEEP UP WITH GROWING MKT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARIA PLANS TO KEEP UP WITH GROWING MKT.

text.p: Hungaria Biztosito Rt, the wholly owned unit of Germany's Allianz AG , plans to maintain its leading position in Hungary's growing insurance market, company officials said on Monday.
"We aim at a 32 to 33 percent share of (the country's total) insurance premium," Mihaly Patai, Hungaria's President and CEO told a news conference following the company's annual general meeting.
In 1996, with an insurance premium income of 49.94 billion forints, Hungaria had a 32.6 percent share of a market worth 153 billion forints, Patai said.
Figures released by Hungaria put AB-Aegon in second place with a 23.2 percent market share and Providencia Rt third with 11.6 percent.
Patai said last year's main achievement was that Hungaria managed to eliminate losses caused by its motor insurance business which still operates under state-controlled prices.
"Due to successful crisis management, we achieved a break-even in the CASCO (motor insurance) sector," Patai said.
He added that according to government officials, motor insurance prices will be gradually liberalised by the year 2000.
Motor insurance accounted for 69.94 percent of Hungaria's premium revenues last year, followed by industrial and international insurance with 15.45 percent.

Patai added that the company also planned to keep up the growth rate of its pension insurance customers, the number of which grew from zero in June 1996 when the fund was set up to 22,000 at the end of the year.
"We would like to remain the fastest-growing pension fund," he said.

Patai said the company, after doubling its life insurance premium revenues last year to 2.66 billion forints, carving out a 5.5 percent market share, plans to increase its share to some eight percent.
"We expect the Hungarian life insurance market to outpace growth in other insurance sectors, growing an annual 40 percent over the next years," Patai said.
Hungaria's sole owner, Allianz said earlier it was prepared to invest some four billion forints in life insurance growth and a board member said Allianz continued to back this plan.
"We think the company (Hungaria) is very well equipped with money at the moment... but if necessary, money will be available for future investment," Allianz board member Detlev Bremkamp said.
In 1996, Hungaria registered after-tax profit of 4.38 billion forints compared with 3.7 billion in 1995.
The company had 15.992 bilion forints of accrued losses from the years 1991 and 1992.
Allianz bought a 49 percent stake in Hungaria in 1992 and gradually increased its stake in it until it became the sole owner at the end of August 19965.
